_comment: Stage D keys are a single integer: {"seed_universe": s}. Training seeds are drawn FRESH every generation from [1, 800000); the eval seeds below live in a disjoint block at 900000+, so a training draw can never collide with an eval world. That disjointness is what makes the generalisation gap meaningful - it is the first rung where train and held-out are different WORLDS rather than different keys into the same fixed set.

key_shape.seed_universe: int; the whole universe is a pure function of it

dispatch.rule: sample 8 distinct fresh seeds from [1, 800000) every generation
dispatch.note: This is the first rung where the fleet's DIVERSITY argument applies (plan.md 5.3): through A-C the eight sandboxes justify themselves on throughput and gradient variance alone, because only action sampling varied. Here each sandbox is genuinely a different universe.
